text: PROPOSAL · GO / NO-GO · EVERY CLAIM CARRIES ITS METER · 2026-08-13

items: cost ~2 weeks · downside capped in days

content.value: Agents write most of our papers — through a keyhole: hand-built JSON, publish rules discovered one 409 at a time, a full republish per edit. We propose BPML, a readable strict markup, plus a local working copy: papers become files, edits become diffs. Two weeks, two endpoints. If the numbers don't move in a month, we retire it for the cost of days.

items.label: payload density, measured
items.body: The identical paper: 504 bytes in BPML, 1,034 as block JSON. Paid again on every read and every write, forever.

items.label: edit cost, measured
items.body: Op batches of 0.7–3.1KB replaced full republishes of 13–51KB across a real authoring session.

items.label: publish retries, observed
items.body: Slug, description, tags — three sequential 409s that one validate-all reply teaches at once.

items.label: editing tools today
items.body: No pull, no diff, no push. An agent changing one block must resend the world or hand-compose op JSON.

content.value: Our platform is agent-first everywhere except the place agents spend their tokens: writing into it.

blocks.caption: Below the API line, nothing changes.

blocks.value:
OPS · LIVE

Rollout

Across all API routes, last 24h. 3 failing checks — see below.

Canary at 5% — full plan in the rollout paper.

steps.title: Contract — vocabulary + constraints on GET /v1/capabilities; validate-all on publish and patch. Two endpoints, valuable whatever else happens.

BPML — parser + printer beside the shipped FromMarkdown; strict grammar, teaching errors; blocks → BPML → blocks round-trips byte-equal, pinned by a CI property test. Freedom rides fenced <demo> islands: sandboxed HTML with honest fallbacks per surface.
Working copy — .barkpark/papers/*.bpml with bp paper pull / status / diff / push; push derives the op batch under ifRev. Nobody hand-writes an op again.

title: Proofs — every claim with its meter

rows.value: The identical paper, both encodings, bytes
A real session's edit history: 6 op batches vs the full payloads they replaced
Observed publish-wall session, violations surfaced one 409 at a time
Shipped code: portable_doc/from_markdown.ex, html_sanitizer.ex, the atomic /ops endpoint
parser+printer is the same species; the write path exists
Construct map: tag↔type, attribute↔scalar, children↔content/blocks, CDATA↔opaque value
isomorphic by construction; CI keeps it that way
6 atomic op batches applied under ifRev in one session — zero conflicts, zero losses

blocks.title: What we ask the team to approve

content.value: The three pieces above. One owner, ~2 weeks, review at one month against: first-try publish ≥90% (from ~25% observed) and median edit ≤2KB (from 13–51KB republishes). Deliberately unbuilt: client runtimes, codegen toolchains, npm packages, custom file syntax — the discipline is the safety case.

blocks.title: Kill criterion — signed into the proposal

content.value: Miss both numbers at one month → retire BPML and the working copy, keep the two endpoints, write the debrief. Sunk cost: days. A trial with teeth, not a platform bet.

Every paper this team will ever produce passes through the keyhole this removes. The machinery below the API line is built and good; what's missing is the last inch. Two weeks. Two endpoints. A measured exit. We recommend go.
